title: Order of dipole moments of BF3, NH4+, NF3 and NH3 from bond and lone-pair moments
summary: Four species sit in a sample tray between two charged plates. Press start and the bench does the rest: it builds each species in 3D from VSEPR, draws every bond dipole and the lone-pair moment, slides them tip to tail to find the resultant, then switches on the field and reads the torque on the molecule. BF3 and NH4+ do not twist at all, NF3 barely, NH3 strongly - the bars line up in order and the answer is revealed. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Dipole moment - vector sum of bond and lone-pair moments
subtopics: Lone-pair (atomic) dipole on the central atom
VSEPR shapes: trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal pyramidal
Vector addition of bond moments; cancellation by symmetry
NH3 versus NF3: lone pair reinforcing or opposing the bond moments
Dipole moment of a symmetric ion about its centre
Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field, tau = pE sin(theta)
concepts: A bond between atoms of different electronegativity is polar; its dipole points (chemists' crossed arrow) from the delta-plus to the delta-minus atom
A lone pair on the central atom puts extra negative charge on one side of it and carries a moment of its own, pointing from the atom out into the pair
The dipole moment of a molecule is the vector sum of its bond and lone-pair moments, so the shape decides whether they add or cancel
BF3 is trigonal planar (3 bond pairs, no lone pair): three equal B-F moments at 120 degrees sum to exactly zero even though each bond is strongly polar
NH4+ is tetrahedral (4 bond pairs, no lone pair): four equal N-H moments to the corners of a tetrahedron sum to zero; the ion's charge is symmetric about N so it has no dipole about its centre
In a trigonal pyramid the sideways parts of the three bond moments cancel and 3 mu_b cos(beta) survives along the axis, with cos^2(beta) = (1 + 2 cos alpha)/3
In NH3 the N-H moments point toward N, the same way as the lone pair, so they add: 1.47 D measured
In NF3 the N-F moments point toward F, away from the lone pair, so they nearly cancel: 0.23 D measured, although N-F is the more polar bond
A dipole in a uniform field feels a torque pE sin(theta) and turns its negative end toward the positive plate; the peak torque divided by E gives the dipole moment
formulas: mu_molecule = | sum of bond moments + lone-pair moments |  (vectors)
mu_bond ~ kappa (chi_A - chi_B), kappa = 1 D per Pauling unit
cos^2(beta) = (1 + 2 cos alpha) / 3  (pyramid, bond angle alpha)
mu(NH3) = 3 mu_NH cos(beta) + mu_lp;  mu(NF3) = | mu_lp - 3 mu_NF cos(beta) |
tau = mu E sin(theta);  mu = tau_max / E

derivedQuantities.option_B: needs BF3 < NH4+ - both are exactly zero
derivedQuantities.option_C: puts NH4+ below BF3 and NF3 above NH3
derivedQuantities.option_D: needs BF3 < NH4+ and NH3 < NF3 - the order you get by forgetting the lone pair

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: VSEPR shapes, bond moments from electronegativity, lone-pair moment on N, vector sum

Symbolic: sympy summed the bond vectors for each VSEPR geometry with the bond moment as a symbol - BF3 and NH4+ vanish identically; the pyramid gives 3m cos(beta) + L (NH3-type) and L - 3m cos(beta) (NF3-type), with cos^2(beta) = (1 + 2 cos alpha)/3 checked against the vectors
Model with Pauling electronegativities, 1 D per unit difference, a 1.0 D lone pair and angles 107/102 degrees: NH3 1.938 D, NF3 0.244 D, BF3 = NH4+ = 0

Robustness: NF3 < NH3 for any lone-pair moment above 0.153 D, for every angle pair NH3 100-110 x NF3 98-106 degrees, and for kappa 0.5-1.5 D per unit; with no lone pair the order flips (option D's trap); BF3 and NH4+ stay exactly zero for any electronegativities
Measured gas-phase values (NCERT: NH3 4.90e-30 C m = 1.47 D, NF3 0.80e-30 C m = 0.24 D; BF3 and NH4+ zero) give the same order
Quantum chemistry: B3LYP/aug-cc-pVDZ (pyscf) at experimental geometries gives BF3 0.000, NH4+ 0.000, NF3 0.197, NH3 1.522 D, with the negative end of NF3 on the fluorine side
Independent numeric script tests/verify_p1q03.py: 28 of 28 checks pass and the answer is (A)

The page computes each resultant as a vector sum, reads it back from the torque meter as tau_max/E, ranks the four and picks the option letter at run time by matching the order against the printed options

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q03.js drives the whole page: optional inputs with empty, invalid, negative, zero and out-of-range values, the automatic run from one START to the reveal, torque zero for BF3 and NH4+ and non-zero for NF3 and NH3, every calculation line in order, the reveal and its blink, replay, pause, reset, a custom run with the lone pair switched off (no printed option), classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries, and the real app shell opening it
Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q3 -> (A)
verification.note: Built to the streamlined specification: no prediction stage, one START, an automatic run, then a detailed solution and a how-to-use section. The question prints no numbers, so the pre-filled 'question values' are the standard data it relies on - Pauling electronegativities, a 1.0 D lone-pair moment on N and the VSEPR bond angles. The simple bond-moment model over-estimates NH3 (1.94 vs 1.47 D) but gives the measured order, which is what the question asks.

interactivity: A dipole bench drawn as a dark lab chamber: a sample holder between a positive and a negative plate, a torque meter, a species card and a sample tray of four
Each species is built in 3D from VSEPR and turns slowly so its shape can be seen: trigonal planar BF3, tetrahedral NH4+, pyramidal NF3 and NH3 with its lone-pair lobe
Bond dipoles appear one by one as blue crossed arrows toward the delta-minus atom, with delta labels; the lone-pair moment appears as an orange arrow
The arrows slide tip to tail while the atoms fade back: for BF3 and NH4+ the chain closes (sum 0), for NF3 and NH3 a green resultant appears

The plates charge, field lines flow, and the molecule is released at 90 degrees: NH3 swings round hard, NF3 barely, BF3 and NH4+ not at all; the torque meter needle and a live tau-theta graph follow it

Every input optional and pre-filled with the standard data: electronegativities of H, B, N and F, the lone-pair moment of N and both bond angles, with steppers and per-field resets; empty or invalid entries fall back with an inline note; USING QUESTION VALUES / USING CUSTOM VALUES badge; RESET TO QUESTION VALUES
One START runs the whole experiment automatically: prepare, four species (build, bond dipoles, lone pair, vector sum, field, record), rank, calculate, EXPERIMENT COMPLETE and the reveal
A bar chart of the measured dipole moments that re-orders itself into the answer with '=' and '<' signs, then overlays the measured values for the real molecules
A calculation panel that writes each vector sum, the torque-meter check tau_max = mu E, the order, the literature check and the matching option as the run produces them
A measurement log with shape, bond moment, lone pair, axial sum, vector sum, peak torque and tau/E for each species
Status indicator (preparing, running, analysing, calculation complete, experiment complete) and a stage strip
The reveal dims the laboratory, flashes, sprays OPTION (A) inside an ANSWER frame with CONGRATULATIONS, ANSWER FOUND and the order, and blinks the header answer once
Custom values run the same experiment; switching the lone pair off lets NF3 overtake NH3 and the reveal says no printed option matches
Pause, 1x / 2x, replay, reset, and a classroom mode that hides the inputs and enlarges the experiment, graphs and equations
A detailed solution that points back to what the experiment showed, a distractor audit, a verification block, and an eight-step how-to-use section
